newsitem.title: USA: Ross expected back in U.S. in two days.
newsitem.headline: Ross expected back in U.S. in two days.

text.p: U.S. Mideast envoy Dennis Ross is expected back in Washington within two days after security discussions with Israelis and Palestinians aimed at resuming peace negotiations, the State Department said on Monday.
"I think it's a matter of ... one or two more days probably, not too much longer than that," spokesman James Rubin told reporters.

Rubin would not say if meetings arranged by Ross between Israeli and Palestinan officials concerning the July 30 suicide bombing of Jerusalem's main Jewish market were enough for Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to formally decide to visit the region this month.

After Ross returns, "we will take a look at what's happened. We will take a look at what we think we can contribute. And on that basis, we will have announcements to make about a trip if that's her decision," he said.

Rubin said while the two sides came a step closer to reviving security ties during Ross' mission, Washington had not seen the 100 percent effort to crack down on militant groups by Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat that Albright has demanded.
But he stressed "that's not something we're going to be able to declare today or tomorrow or the next day, because it's specifically intended to be a standard that is met over time."

Within hours of his arrival in Israel on Sunday, Ross had brought together Arafat and Israeli officials for the first time since two Arab suicide bombers brought carnage to the market. Sixteen people died.
A second meeting, among Israeli, Palestinian and American security officials, took place on Monday.

The fact that the experts are "getting down to the nitty-gritty ... (of) what needs to be done is a step in the right direction. But the extent of that progress will be determined by actions, not meetings," Rubin said.
"What we're going to be watching for ... is to see whether the commitments made are commitments kept," he added.
In a speech last week, Albright said "some progress" on security must be demonstrated before she will make her first Middle East trip as Secretary of State.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has accused Arafat of having a "revolving door" for militants in his prisons and has conditioned resumed peace talks and an easing of sanctions imposed on the West Bank and Gaza Strip after the bombings on a crackdown by the Palestinian Authority.
